newsitem.title: USA: Global electronics equipment market to grow - study.
newsitem.headline: Global electronics equipment market to grow - study.

text.p: The worldwide electronics equipment production market will grow 9.5 percent in 1997, reaching revenues of $930.5 billion, according to a study by Dataquest, a market research and consulting firm.
The market's five-year compound annual growth rate is expected to be near eight percent, with revenue reaching $1.2 trillion by 2001, the study said.

"The market will be fueled in particular by an increase in PCs, data storage devices, wireless and networking communications equipment, digital consumer products, and automobile features taking advantage of distributed control designs," said Xavier Pucel, an industry analyst at Dataquest.

Data processing is the application expected to most drive the electronic equipment industry, with a projected $312 billion in 1997. Communications applications follow with $211 billion in 1997 and then comes the consumer applications market, which is expected to reach $169 billion.
The Americas region will lead the rest of the world in production revenue through the rest of this decade, Dataquest said, with revenue of more than $335 billion in 1997.
Dataquest is a Gartner Group Inc unit.
